utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. The Chamber has been informed that Mr. Karadzic is still ill; however, given that the Chamber hasn't received any official report, it would like to receive a medical report from the Registry as to the current health situation of the accused and also as well as as to when he would be able to be back to the courtroom. That said, while the Chamber cannot be composed next week, the Chamber has in mind taking a deposition of certain witnesses, in particular those from -- those experts from Australia or the US by one of the member of the Bench who would be available. So I'm -- I'd like to inquire to the parties as to its feasibility and possibility or any observations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, what -- we would hope that Dr. Karadzic would be better tomorrow and that the testimony could be heard before the Trial Chamber, and we would oppose the taking of any depositions because it seems to us that that circumvents Rule 15 bis and it's not intended for that purpose. So we would prefer that -- we do everything we can to see that the witnesses can testify before the recess, but we would not be in favour of any depositions under those circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So could you elaborate on the reason why it circumvents the spirit of 15 bis. It's a deposition and then -- which is to be reported back to the Chamber and the Chamber can consider the situation whether to admit it or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, I understand that. But when the reason for taking a deposition is the fact that the Bench can't be composed, then it seems like that's circumventing Rule 15 bis, because Rule 15 bis basically provides the way to proceed when a Chamber cannot be composed. And I haven't looked at the deposition rule, but it seems like it requires some kind of special circumstances or interests of justice, and I don't think that the absence of a member of the Bench would constitute those kind of interests of justice or special circumstances that could justify a deposition. Normally depositions are justified by the unavailability of the witness or the inability of the witness to either be heard by videolink or to come to The Hague. So our position would be that that is not -- that a deposition under those circumstances wouldn't be in the interests of justice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There are certain precedents in the -- at the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I know it's been done before and I believe it's usually been done without objection, but in this case we do object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And if you could let us know the availability of the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Only Dr. -- actually, I myself won't be available beginning on Friday morning, but Dr. Karadzic will be here as soon as he's healthy and he's the only one on the Defence team who would be able to conduct the deposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, we would, of course, in response to Mr. Robinson, we want to take the opportunity as quickly as possible to review the relevant jurisprudence, but we are also aware that depositions have been conducted in what appear to be similar circumstances. By way of logistics, since the Court mentioned the composition of the Trial Chamber next week, it's probably important for me to note that two of the experts, Witnesses Lawrence and Haglund, cannot be here next week. So they will be -- they will have to leave by the end of this week in any event. So that may figure into the Court's calculations in some manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. And the Chamber will consider the issue and will inform the parties of the result accordingly. There's one matter about which we would like to issue an oral ruling now. It's related to the Prosecution's application regarding the report on use of time in the trial filed yesterday. In the application, the Prosecution requests the Trial Chamber to direct the Registry to provide a breakdown of the time calculations for each witness who testified during the 1st to the 30th of November, 2011, and it requests to be allowed to file an application challenging the time used by it within seven days from the receipt of the breakdown of the time calculations. The Chamber hereby grants both requests, orders the Registry to provide the time statistics for November to the Prosecution as soon as practicable and orders the Prosecution to file its challenge within seven days of the receipt of these time statistics. And further, I would like the report I referred to earlier today at the outset of the hearing to be filed hopefully by the end of today. The hearing is now -- yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: One more possibility for consideration and I'm only throwing it out by way of the potential options of dealing with the problematic situation we have encountered and that is whether or not the stand-by counsel can be considered for cross-examination on Thursday and Friday. So it, at least, seems worthy of some consideration and I put it out in that spirit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: One final question for you, Mr. Tieger, is if we would be able to sit tomorrow, who will be the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It would be Mr. Riedlmayer, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. The hearing is now adjourned until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 8th day of December, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 9.24 a.m.,
